acceptance: Each deep-reviewer backend is either restored to working order or its outage is recorded with an owner and expected resolution.

A muse-authored PR can receive a deep review from at least one backend without requiring a same-family exception, or the same-family skip is documented as intended with the stand-in path as the explicit fallback.
The oracle-review required check passes on a clean PR without owner intervention. (Observed failing state: PR 3170 verdict pending with zero findings, 2026-10-19.)
context: Observed 2026-10-19 on PR 3170: the oracle verdict came back pending with no findings because every backend was unavailable: claude-deep absent (error), codex-deep disabled (no OpenAI API quota), gemini-deep disabled (unverified harness), muse-deep skipped (same model family as the PR author). With three backends down and the fourth skipping same-family authors, every agent-authored PR falls back to owner stand-in attestation, which defeats the gate. Owner/ops decision; no code change is assumed.
description: Three of four oracle deep-reviewer backends are unavailable (claude-deep errors, codex-deep has no quota, gemini-deep is disabled) and muse-deep skips PRs authored by the same model family, so agent-authored PRs cannot receive any deep review and the oracle-review required check can only pass via owner stand-in. Restore at least one backend or record an explicit policy decision that stand-in attestation is the normal path for agent-authored PRs.
